fallen_sign: A brass planet the size of a house lies dented in its own crater. Three families have put up three 'PRIVATE' signs on it.
fallen_notice: A notice: PLANET RETRIEVAL - CONTACT THE GILT HOUSE. Below, in another hand: OR ME. CHEAPER. - L.
brine_sign: Under the Mirror Flats the old lake keeps its dead in salt. Halloran keeps his barrels beside them. Both are counted daily.
brine_stencil: A barrel stencil: PROPERTY OF HALLORAN SALT. A second stencil underneath: AND SO ARE YOU.
brine_niche: A saint's niche, empty but for a price list. 'Pinch: 5. Bag: 50. Miracle: ask.'
chapel_pews: The drowned chapel. Salt has crusted the pews white. Someone has scratched SING LOUDER into the back row.
chapel_hymns: A hymn board. The same hymn number, every week, for twelve years.
cellar_sign: The Gilt House keeps its wine, its gold and its relatives down here. Not always in that order.
cellar_rack: A cask rack. Each cask is chalked with a year and a name. Cask forty-one says only: KNOCK.
strong_wills: The strongroom. Five drawers, one per Gilt child, each with a will inside. Each will leaves everything to the drawer's owner.
strong_debts: A ledger titled DEBTS OWED TO THE HOUSE. It is very thick. A thinner one beside it, titled DEBTS THE HOUSE OWES, is blank.
antidote_wait: Benno: The herbalist on the White Stair mixes antidotes. And the cellar clerk under the Sunfall Terraces signs for every bottle.

lines: Benno: The order is in my name? Well. I did say nobody keeps me alive for free. I pay myself.
Benno: I taste, I live, I add the seasoning afterwards. Lady Seraphine pays per guest. Lord Aurek is the main course.
Benno: And now you know the recipe. Recipes are family secrets. You are not family.
Food Taster Benno: I taste for Lord Aurek. Three thousand meals, eleven poisons, not one funeral. Mine, I mean.
Food Taster Benno: Someone keeps slipping antidote into my soup. Nobody in this family keeps anyone alive for free. Find out who.

antidote_wenna_after: Herbalist Wenna: I sell poison too. Same shelf. I just turn the labels round.

lines: Herbalist Wenna: Antidote, a flask a week, for the Gilt kitchen. Paid in advance, which is how you know it's for someone important.
Herbalist Wenna: The bottles go down to the Gilt Cellars. Ask the clerk whose name is on the order.

antidote_tobin_after: Cellar Clerk Tobin: I count bottles. Bottles never lie. People empty them and then lie.

lines: Cellar Clerk Tobin: The antidote? Ordered by the taster himself. Weekly. He drinks it before every meal he tests.
Cellar Clerk Tobin: Odd habit for a man paid to fall over. Nine guests have died after he said 'delicious'.

antidote_benno_fork_after: Benno: I've retired. Now I only taste my own cooking. It's the only meal I trust.

lines: You take Benno's tasting kit: three tonics and a little spoon engraved 'NOT MINE'.
antidote_benno_fork_loot.action: set_flag q4_antidote_paid; give_item max_tonic 3; quest_stage q4_antidote 4

antidote_benno_fork_intro: Benno: Say 'delicious'. Everyone says it before they fall over.
antidote_benno_fork_defeat: Benno: Bitter. Very bitter. I'd send it back.
Benno: Fine. Tell Aurek. He'll hire a taster for his taster.
brass_planet_wait: Lio: It lies past Orrery Ridge, in a crater. Nan picks scrap there. And Notary Fenwick on the White Stair keeps the deeds.

lines: Lio: Three deeds? Ah. Yes. A planet is very big. It seemed a shame to sell it only once.
Lio: Collector Ambrose of the Gilt House is in the crater now, to take it. Beat him, and the other two families get nothing. Then we split.
Lio: The crater, past Orrery Ridge. Go on. I'll keep your half warm.
Lio: You beat Ambrose? Wonderful. Here is your half. Half of the advance. Half of the advance minus expenses.
brass_planet_reward.action: set_flag q4_brass_planet_paid; give_item revival_leaf 2; quest_stage q4_brass_planet 4; betrayal hs_brass_planet

lines: Lio: I'm selling the crater next. It has a lovely view of the planet.
Apprentice Lio: The missing planet of the Great Orrery! It fell off the ridge in a storm. I'm the only one who knows where.
Apprentice Lio: Fetch proof that it's still lying there, and I'll sell it back to the Gilt House. Fifty-fifty. I'm told I have an honest face.

brass_planet_nan_after: Nan: I sell the dents separately. Very popular with the Gilt cousins.

lines: Scrap Picker Nan: The planet? Big brass ball, dented, smells of money. It's in the crater. Three families have already come to look at it.
Scrap Picker Nan: Each one had a deed for it. Ask the notary how a ball gets three owners.

brass_planet_fenwick_after: Fenwick: Every deed on this stair is legal. Some are even true.

lines: Notary Fenwick: Three deeds for one planet, all sold by the same seller. Lovely handwriting. Very honest face.
Notary Fenwick: The seller signed as 'Lio, apprentice'. I stamped all three. I am paid by the stamp, not by the truth.

brass_planet_ambrose_after: Ambrose: I collect. You are on a list now. It's a short list. It gets shorter.
brass_planet_ambrose_defeat: Ambrose: Keep it, then. Lio sold it to me with your name as the courier. The other two families have your name as well.
Ambrose: In this family, the one who carries the parcel pays for it.
brass_planet_ambrose_lose: Ambrose: The crater keeps what falls into it. Come back when you've grown a little.

lines: Ambrose: This planet belongs to the Gilt House. So does the crater. And, as of now, your afternoon.

brass_planet_dita_after: Dita: Dust is honest. It settles on everyone.

lines: Sweeper Dita: I sweep under the brass arms. Last week I swept up three deed copies with Lio's name. And yours, as courier. Each time.
Sweeper Dita: Keep the copies. I only keep the dust.

ledger_brass_planet: Apprentice Lio sold the Great Orrery's missing planet to three families, each time with your name as the courier.
brass_planet_caught: You show Lio the sweeper's copies: three deeds, three families, your name as courier on each.
Lio: ...You read the small print. Nobody reads the small print. Fine. Here is the real half. Don't tell the other half of me.
brass_planet_struck: Lio: Oh, and the other two families are outside. I told them you have the planet. You do, technically. You beat the man holding it.
planet_buyers_defeat: Planet Buyer: Keep your planet. We'll buy the next one. There is always a next one.
planet_buyers_lose: The buyers take your coins as a deposit on the planet you don't own.
salt_skim_wait: Imre: Jost rolls barrels in the Brine Catacombs, east of the flats. And Hanne dives in the drowned chapel below.

lines: Imre: A neat hand? Well. Mine is the neatest on the flats. It's my one vanity.
Imre: Halloran pays me in salt and docks me in coin. So I water his salt and blame the boy. Everyone wins except Jost.
Imre: You were supposed to find Jost guilty. Now I have to write you off. I'm very good at writing things off.
Bookkeeper Imre: I keep Halloran's salt books. The barrels leave full and arrive light. Somebody skims.
Imre: I suspect my apprentice, Jost. Find proof. Halloran deducts the losses from my wages, and my wages are mostly losses already.

salt_skim_jost_after: Jost: Roll, roll, roll. The salt doesn't care who owns it.

lines: Jost: A tip, for the road: behind the third cask down here, Halloran keeps a dry stash. Nobody guards it at night. Probably.

salt_skim_betray: Behind the third cask wait two of Halloran's salt guards, and Jost, collecting a finder's fee. For you.
jost_guards_defeat: Salt Guard: The boy said you'd be easy. The boy lies. We'll take it out of his barrels.
jost_guards_lose: The guards fine you for trespass on company salt.
ledger_salt_skim: Barrel Boy Jost sold you a tip about Halloran's stash, then sold you to the guards who were waiting there.
salt_skim_rewarded: Behind the third cask: a dry stash, unguarded, as promised. Jost tips his cap. A revival leaf was going spare.
salt_skim_kept: Behind the third cask: salt. Only salt. Jost shrugs. 'I said probably.'

lines: Barrel Boy Jost: Skimming? Me? I can't even count to a barrel. I roll them, I don't open them.
Jost: The light barrels go down to the chapel before they're weighed. Ask Hanne. And don't tell Imre I talked.

salt_skim_hanne_after: Hanne: I dive for what the lake forgot. It forgot a lot. It had help.

lines: Salt Diver Hanne: The light barrels? They come down here half full and go back up with water from the chapel font. Salt water weighs like salt.
Hanne: The man who brings them signs the book with a very neat hand. Bookkeepers have very neat hands.

salt_skim_imre_ink_after: Imre: Jost has my job now. He can't count. Halloran says it's an improvement.

lines: You take Imre's cash box. Inside: three tonics and a second set of books, much more honest than the first.
salt_skim_imre_ink_loot.action: set_flag q4_salt_skim_paid; give_item strong_tonic 3; quest_stage q4_salt_skim 4

salt_skim_imre_ink_intro: Imre: Debit: one testimony. Credit: nothing. The books will balance.
salt_skim_imre_ink_defeat: Imre: Overdrawn. Me. I've never been overdrawn.
Imre: Take the books to Halloran. He'll fire me, then hire me back cheaper. That's how he hired me the first time.
two_lanterns_wait: Sabeth: Ledger girl Pia keeps Veronne's book on the Lantern Span. My sister Rosamund guides at the Great Orrery. She hears every rumour first.

lines: Sabeth: Konrad. Of course. He always said he'd never let me go. I thought it was romantic.
Sabeth: He waits on the Span tonight. Beat him before he walks me to the railing.
Sabeth: The Lantern Span, the island in the middle. Mind the railing. It's mostly decorative.
Sabeth: He's beaten? Then my plate can wait. Take these, for your trouble. And for your discretion.
two_lanterns_reward.action: set_flag q4_two_lanterns_paid; give_item guard_brew 3; quest_stage q4_two_lanterns 4; betrayal hs_two_lanterns

lines: Sabeth: I've engraved a plate for Konrad anyway. Just in case. I'm an optimist.
Engraver Sabeth: I engrave the plates under the lanterns. Today an order came in for a new plate. The name on it is mine.
Sabeth: Prepaid. Somebody has booked my fall. Find out who. I'd like to cancel.

two_lanterns_pia_after: Pia: Black ink for the living, red for the rest. I go through a lot of red.

lines: Ledger Girl Pia: Sabeth's plate? Red column, prepaid, signed by 'a loving husband'. Loving husbands are our best customers.
Pia: Ask her sister. Sisters always know whose husband is loving whom.

two_lanterns_rosamund_after: Rosamund: The stars don't fall. People do. That's why I work indoors.

lines: Star Guide Rosamund: Konrad? Sabeth's husband? He's been asking which lanterns burn longest. For sentimental reasons, he said.
Rosamund: He waits on the Lantern Span every evening, counting the drop. Tell my sister. Gently. Or not. She never was gentle with me.

two_lanterns_konrad_after: Konrad: I'm moving out. Downstairs. Well away from any stairs.
two_lanterns_konrad_intro: Konrad: You've come from Sabeth. Then you're the other name.
two_lanterns_konrad_defeat: Konrad: The other name, I said. The order had two plates. Mine and the courier's. Sabeth wrote it. I only paid.
Konrad: She wanted me over the railing and you as the one who pushed. One lantern each. Very tidy, my wife.
two_lanterns_yorick_after: Yorick: Shiny plates, short lives. Business is steady.

lines: Plate Polisher Yorick: Two blank plates came in last week, paid together. One for a husband. One for 'the courier'. The order slip is in the engraver's own hand.
Yorick: I polish. I don't read. Except slips. Slips are short.

ledger_two_lanterns: Engraver Sabeth ordered two lantern plates: one for her husband, one for the courier she sent to stop him.
two_lanterns_caught: You lay Yorick's slip on Sabeth's bench: two plates, one for Konrad, one for 'the courier', in her hand.
Sabeth: ...Polishers. They read everything. Fine. Here is the courier's fee. It was meant for your lantern. Spend it on something cheerful.
two_lanterns_struck: Sabeth: One more thing. The pushers I hired for Konrad are still paid up. Waste not.
plate_pushers_defeat: Pusher: Paid for one fall, got none. Sabeth wants a refund. We want a new line of work.
plate_pushers_lose: The pushers walk you to the railing and stop. They charge extra for the last step.
forged_will_wait: Philippa: The archivist sits in the strongroom of the Gilt Cellars. If he dawdles, the ink seller on Cloudshadow Meadow can vouch for the paper.

lines: Philippa: Practice makes perfect. Father always said so. He'll be proud. When he reads it. If.
Philippa: You're the witness on page three, by the way. Witnesses to Gilt wills have a short shelf life.
Philippa: Meet me in the strongroom. We'll settle the estate.
Gilt Heir Philippa: I'm the fourth child. Fourth children inherit the cutlery and the blame. But Father wrote a new will. In my favour.
Philippa: Have it sealed by the archivist in the Gilt Cellars before my siblings eat it. One of them ate the last one. With mustard.

forged_will_hollis_after: Hollis: I have five wills here from five children. Each leaves everything to the author. Literature.

lines: Archivist Hollis: A new will from Lord Aurek? Hm. The wax is still warm. Lord Aurek has not left his room in a week. His wax is cold.
Hollis: And the ink is meadow violet. Ask the ink seller on Cloudshadow Meadow who bought it.

forged_will_marla_after: Marla: Ink is cheap. Signatures are expensive. I sell the cheap part.

lines: Ink Seller Marla: Meadow violet? One bottle, last week, to a young lady with a Gilt brooch and a very steady hand.
Marla: She also bought a practice pad. Lord Aurek's signature, forty times. The last ten were perfect.

forged_will_philippa_will_after: Philippa: Father read my will. He laughed so hard he added me to his. Under 'cutlery'.

lines: You take the forged will and Philippa's travel case: three brews and a fork with somebody else's crest.
forged_will_philippa_will_loot.action: set_flag q4_forged_will_paid; give_item focus_brew 3; quest_stage q4_forged_will 4

forged_will_philippa_will_defeat: Philippa: Contested. My will. By a witness. The cheek.
Philippa: Take it. Burn it. I'll write another. I've got thirty perfect signatures left.
forged_will_philippa_will_lose: Philippa: Witnessed and signed. Go and rest. You look predeceased.

lines: Philippa: Page three, line two: 'The witness predeceased the testator.' Let's make it true.

cask_41_wait: Gerti: The cooper in the Gilt Cellars knows every cask. And the old taster on Orrery Ridge knows every vintage.

lines: Gerti: Uncle Bertrand? In a cask? For eleven years? The family said he'd gone abroad.
Gerti: Let him out. He's owed his share of the house. Quietly. The strongroom key opens cask forty-one.
Gerti: The strongroom of the Gilt Cellars. Bring a corkscrew. A big one.
Gerti: Bertrand went back into his cask? Fine. Saves the family a room. Here, for the corkscrew.
cask_41_reward.action: set_flag q4_cask_41_paid; give_item dash_brew 3; quest_stage q4_cask_41 4; betrayal hs_cask_41

lines: Gerti: The Gilt wine tastes nuttier this year. Nobody complains.
Vineyard Hand Gerti: The Gilt wine has a secret ingredient. It talked too much, they say. Well. One cask in the cellar knocks back.
Gerti: Find out who's in it. Quietly. Wine doesn't like noise, and neither does the family.

cask_41_mattheus_after: Mattheus: I feed it through the bunghole. Soup, mostly. It complains about the soup.

lines: Cooper Mattheus: Cask forty-one? It knocks twice for yes and once for 'more bread'. It's been knocking for eleven years.
Mattheus: Eleven years ago, the vintage of the Great Quarrel. Ask the old taster on Orrery Ridge who went missing that year.

cask_41_albrecht_after: Albrecht: I spit, I never swallow. In wine and in family matters.

lines: Old Taster Albrecht: The Great Quarrel vintage? That was the year Uncle Bertrand, Aurek's brother, vanished owing money to every family on the plateau.
Albrecht: The wine from that year had a nutty finish. And a faint aftertaste of uncle.

cask_41_bertrand_after: Bertrand: Knock twice for yes. Once for more bread.
cask_41_bertrand_defeat: Bertrand: I went into that cask myself, you know. Cheaper than paying. I'll go back in. The soup was free.
cask_41_bertrand_lose: Bertrand: There. Breathe. Every vintage needs to breathe.

lines: Bertrand: Free! Eleven years in oak. I'm wonderfully aged. Now, about my creditors: you'll do as a first payment.

cask_41_fenna_after: Fenna: I pick the grapes. I don't pick sides.

lines: Vine Girl Fenna: Gerti? She's Bertrand's daughter. She told the cousins someone was coming to open his cask. They want to catch whoever does.
Fenna: The cousins pay for intruders by the head. Gerti needs the money. Her father owes everyone.

ledger_cask_41: Vineyard Hand Gerti sent you to open her father's cask and then sold you to the cousins, by the head.
cask_41_caught: You tell Gerti what the vine girl said. Gerti counts the cousins coming up the terraces and changes her mind.
Gerti: Fine. I'll tell them you were never here. Take this. It's the only bottle in the cellar with nobody in it.
cask_41_struck: Gerti: Oh, cousins! Here's the one who opened Uncle's cask. Per head, wasn't it?
cask_cousins_defeat: Gilt Cousin: Per head, she said. We'll pay her nothing. Families are complicated.
cask_cousins_lose: The cousins fine you for disturbing a vintage.
true_stars_wait: Ennis: Arno watches the meadow through his telescope on Orrery Ridge. And the goat girl here sees everyone who crosses.

lines: Ennis: My wife? Wanda? Making my horoscopes come true? Oh, Wanda.
Ennis: She's on the meadow, delivering 'a sudden change of fortune'. Stop her before she ruins my reputation for accuracy. I mean, before she hurts someone.
Ennis: The west side of the meadow, by the trees. Her stars are always in the west.
Ennis: Wanda is stopped? A tragedy. My accuracy will suffer. Here, take these. Your horoscope: long life. For now.
true_stars_reward.action: set_flag q4_true_stars_paid; give_item wake_bell 3; quest_stage q4_true_stars 4

lines: Ennis: I've hired a new assistant. Young. Ambitious. Her stars are very precise.
Horoscope Seller Ennis: My horoscopes come true. All of them. 'Beware of heights': fell off a terrace. 'A stranger brings news': poisoned by a courier.
Ennis: Business has never been better, and I am terrified. Find out who makes my stars come true.

true_stars_arno_after: Arno: I see everything from up here. Nobody ever looks back up.

lines: Arno: With a better lens I could see her face. Lend me 800 coins? I'll pay you back. Probably with interest.

true_stars_betray: Arno spends your coins on a lens and sells the first thing he sees through it: your face, to the woman in the shawl. Her friends come calling.
arno_watchers_defeat: Watcher: Your horoscope said 'a quiet week'. Ennis will have to print a correction.
arno_watchers_lose: The watchers take your coins. The horoscope said you'd lose some money.
ledger_true_stars: Telescope Boy Arno borrowed your coins for a better lens and sold your face with the first look through it.
true_stars_rewarded: Arno pays you back with interest and a sketch of the woman's face. It looks a lot like Ennis's wedding portrait.
true_stars_kept: Arno pays you back, to the coin. 'Interest is for people who own banks,' he says.

lines: Telescope Boy Arno: I saw it. A woman in a star-pattern shawl follows every customer of Ennis. Then the customer has a very bad day.
Arno: Will you pay me for what I saw? Information on this plateau is never free.

choices.text: Here, a coin for your trouble.

true_stars_liv_after: Liv: My goats eat horoscopes. They've lived very long lives.

lines: Goat Girl Liv: The lady in the star shawl? She walks with Ennis's customers and takes a little bag from each. Then she goes home.
Liv: Home is Ennis's house. She kisses him at the door. Goats notice things.

true_stars_wanda_after: Wanda: Your stars say: go home. Mine say: so should I.
true_stars_wanda_intro: Wanda: Your horoscope today: 'an unexpected fight'. I deliver.
true_stars_wanda_defeat: Wanda: Ennis sent you? Ennis writes them. I only deliver. He picks the customers who owe him money.
Wanda: He wanted you to stop me so he could hire a younger star. Marriage.
own_cairn_wait: Ewald: The quarryman at the Fallen Planet cut the stones. And Courier Netta on the Mirror Flats carried the order.

lines: Ewald: Netta talks too much. Yes, I order them. A cairn with no one under it is just a heap.
Ewald: The House pays per finished cairn. You said no to the House the day you came up the funicular. You just didn't notice.
Ewald: Come up the ridge. I've a top stone to lay.
Cairn Builder Ewald: In Whitecairn every cairn is a person who said no to the Gilt House. I build them. Somebody ordered one with your name.
Ewald: Prepaid, with a nice view. I'd like to know who before I lay the top stone. It's a matter of craft.

own_cairn_rolf_after: Rolf: I cut stones for the living. It's steadier work than for the dead. The dead don't order twice.

lines: Quarryman Rolf: Your cairn stones? Cut last week. Good white stone, very flattering. The order came with tea stains.
Rolf: Netta brought it. She carries everything on the plateau. Ask her who gave it to her.

own_cairn_netta_after: Netta: I carry, I don't read. Reading is how couriers end up under cairns.

lines: Courier Netta: The cairn order? I carried it from Whitecairn to the quarry. From Ewald's own workshop. He orders his cairns himself.
Netta: Then the Gilt House pays him per cairn finished. Finished means the name is true. He makes them true.

own_cairn_ewald_stone_after: Ewald: I build garden walls now. Nobody has to be under them. Usually.

lines: You take Ewald's order book. Your page is torn out. Tucked in the spine: a spark drop he was saving for his own cairn.
own_cairn_ewald_stone_loot.action: set_flag q4_own_cairn_paid; give_item spark_drop 1; quest_stage q4_own_cairn 4

own_cairn_ewald_stone_intro: Ewald: Hold still. A cairn is only as straight as the person under it.
own_cairn_ewald_stone_defeat: Ewald: Toppled. My own heap. That's a first.
Ewald: Keep the stones. Build something cheerful. A wall, maybe. Walls are cheerful.
red_column_wait: Wido: Father works the Sunfall Terraces under another name. And the debt clerk in the Gilt Cellars keeps the red pages.

lines: Wido: Father sold his name and left me the bill? ...That's very like him.
Wido: The collector waits at the top of the Span. Beat him and the line stays empty. Please. I'm too young to be red.
Wido: The north end of the Lantern Span. He's the one counting the lanterns.
Wido: He's gone? Thank you! Here, it's all I have. Well. All I have that's not owed.
red_column_reward.action: set_flag q4_red_column_paid; give_item remedy 4; quest_stage q4_red_column 4; betrayal hs_red_column

lines: Wido: I'm learning to keep books. Mostly to see who to blame.
Clerk's Boy Wido: Veronne's toll ledger has a red column for people who fell. My father is in it. He didn't fall. He waves at me from the vineyards.
Wido: Find out why he's in the red. The red column pays out to the family. We never got a coin.

red_column_hal_after: Hal: I'm dead on paper. It's restful. You should try it.

lines: Vine Guard Hal: Wido sent you? My boy. Yes, I'm in the red column. I sold my name to Veronne to get out of my debts. A dead man owes nothing.
Hal: The debts had to go somewhere. Ask Margit in the Gilt Cellars where.

red_column_margit_after: Margit: Red ink, black ink. In the end it's all ink.

lines: Debt Clerk Margit: Hal's debts? Passed to his next of kin, as is proper. The next red line is already written. Wido, son of Hal.
Margit: The Span collector comes for him tonight. He collects the debt or the debtor. He isn't fussy.

red_column_ruprecht_after: Ruprecht: I count lanterns. One day I'll count yours.
red_column_ruprecht_defeat: Ruprecht: Uncollectable. I hate that word.
Ruprecht: The line stays empty tonight. Lines don't stay empty long on this bridge.
red_column_ruprecht_lose: Ruprecht: Paid in part. Go and rest. Interest accrues.

lines: Ruprecht: Wido, son of Hal? No. You're not on my page. Yet. Let's start a new page.

red_column_fey_after: Fey: I light them, I don't read them.

lines: Lantern Girl Fey: Wido paid Margit last night. To move his line. The next red line will carry the name of whoever helped him.
Fey: Kids learn fast up here. Mostly from their fathers.

ledger_red_column: Wido moved his red line in Veronne's toll ledger onto the name of the one who saved him: yours.
red_column_caught: You tell Wido you know about the line he moved. He goes pale, then red, then counts out coins.
Wido: I'll move it again. To an empty name. There are plenty under the lanterns. Here. Don't tell Father. He'd be proud.
red_column_struck: Wido: By the way, the next red line is yours now. I moved mine. The collectors work in pairs.
redline_collectors_defeat: Span Collector: Uncollectable again. Margit will have to use a rubber.
redline_collectors_lose: The collectors take a down payment on your red line.
brake_file_wait: Ulf: The White Stair counters see everyone on the steps at dawn. And Gaspard on the Gilt Span sells files.

lines: Ulf: Gaspard said that? Well. A brake that never breaks pays nothing. A brake that breaks every night pays every morning.
Ulf: Nobody has died. Yet. That's craftsmanship. And now you're going to tell the family, and I'm going to have to put the brakes on you.
Brake Mechanic Ulf: Every night someone files the brakes of the Gilt Funicular. Every morning I fix them. Every morning the family pays me.
Ulf: It can't go on. Someone will get hurt. Probably a passenger. Find the filer for me.

brake_file_kuno_after: Kuno: Eight hundred and thirteen. Fourteen. Don't make me lose count.

lines: Step Counter Kuno: At dawn? One man, every day, coming down from the funicular with metal dust on his sleeves. Step eight hundred and twelve, always.
Kuno: Gaspard on the Gilt Span sells him a new file every week. Ask Gaspard who.

brake_file_gaspard_after: Gaspard: Files, rasps, nail clippers. Everything for the man who wants things thinner.

lines: File Seller Gaspard: A file a week, for six years, to the same man. He says he uses them to fix brakes.
Gaspard: Ulf. Brake mechanic. Lovely man. Never once bought a spanner.

brake_file_ulf_file_after: Ulf: I fix bicycles now. Nobody on the plateau owns a bicycle. It's very peaceful.

lines: You take Ulf's tool roll: three brews and forty-one files, each slightly used.
brake_file_ulf_file_loot.action: set_flag q4_brake_file_paid; give_item power_brew 3; quest_stage q4_brake_file 4

brake_file_ulf_file_defeat: Ulf: Brakes failed. Mine, this time.
Ulf: Tell them, then. They'll hire someone who files twice as fast. Progress.
brake_file_ulf_file_lose: Ulf: There. You'll stop now. Everyone stops eventually.

lines: Ulf: Hold on to something. This is going to be a steep descent.

wedding_blades_wait: Leonore: Posy does the flowers, on Cloudshadow Meadow. And the priest rehearses on the White Stair. Both hear everything.

lines: Leonore: The groom hired Dorian for me? Florian! And I thought he wasn't the romantic type.
Leonore: Yes, I hired myself for him. A bride should be prepared. Now beat Dorian on the Mirror Flats, and Sunday is just a wedding again. Mostly.
Leonore: The north end of the Mirror Flats. He practises his toast there. And his aim.
Leonore: Dorian is beaten? Then Florian lives to say 'I do'. Here, a wedding favour. Don't eat the almonds.
wedding_blades_reward.action: set_flag q4_wedding_blades_paid; give_item max_tonic 2; quest_stage q4_wedding_blades 4

lines: Leonore: We're very happy. We sleep in shifts.
Bride Leonore: I marry Cousin Florian of the Gilt House on Sunday. Gilt weddings have a tradition: somebody always tries to kill the groom.
Leonore: Find out who's been hired this time. I want him alive at least until the vows. After that, the paperwork is simpler.

wedding_blades_posy_after: Posy: Lilies last a week. Gilt marriages, about the same.

lines: Posy: Between us: the groom's cake is poisoned. Carry the bride's cake to his table instead and swap them. Trust me.

wedding_blades_betray: The bride's cake was the poisoned one. As you set it down, the bride's guards seize you for trying to poison the groom. Posy waves from the door.
posy_guards_defeat: Bridal Guard: Fine, you didn't do it. Someone did. Someone always does.
posy_guards_lose: The guards fine you for cake-related conduct.
ledger_wedding_blades: Florist Posy talked you into swapping the wedding cakes, so that you would carry the poison to the groom's table.
wedding_blades_rewarded: You swap the cakes. The groom's cake really was poisoned; the cousin who baked it eats his own slice by mistake and spends the wedding indisposed. Posy slips you a tip from the bouquet budget.
wedding_blades_kept: You swap the cakes. Neither was poisoned. Posy shrugs. 'Rumours are cheaper than arsenic.'

lines: Florist Posy: The Gilt wedding? Lilies for the bride, lilies for the groom, lilies for the funeral after. I order in bulk.
Posy: The priest knows who paid for what. Ask him. And tell me: are you with the bride or the groom?

wedding_blades_aldous_after: Aldous: Till death do them part. In this family, it's a schedule.

lines: Priest Aldous: Two payments for Sunday. One from the groom's side, for 'the removal of the bride after the vows'. One from the bride's side, for the groom, same terms.
Aldous: The bride's man is herself. The groom's man is his best man, Dorian, practising on the Mirror Flats. I marry them anyway. It's a living.

wedding_blades_dorian_after: Dorian: To the happy couple. May they both survive the honeymoon.
wedding_blades_dorian_intro: Dorian: You're from the bride's side. I can tell. You have the look of a guest who isn't staying for dessert.
wedding_blades_dorian_defeat: Dorian: Fine. I'll give a toast instead. It was going to be short anyway.
Dorian: Tell Leonore that Florian paid me with her own dowry. They really are made for each other.
salt_saint_wait: Kaspar: A pilgrim resting at the Fallen Planet heard the Saint sing. And the tomb is somewhere in the drowned chapel below.

lines: Kaspar: She wants fifty-fifty? She's dead. The dead take what they're given.
Kaspar: A living saint is just a girl who sings off key. A dead one is a business. You've seen too much of the business.
Kaspar: Come down the east passage. I'll sell you a pinch for the road.
Relic Seller Kaspar: Relics of the Salt Saint! She wept salt for the lake, and the lake took her. A pinch heals anything. A bag heals more.
Kaspar: My stock is running low. Find the Saint's tomb down here and bring me more of her. Sorry, more of her salt.

salt_saint_ortrud_after: Ortrud: I walked here from Paleshore on my bad knee. The knee says it was not worth it.

lines: Pilgrim Ortrud: The Salt Saint? I bought a pinch of her for my knee. The knee is the same. The pinch tasted of kitchen.
Ortrud: But I heard singing under the flats. Someone very alive, very bored, in the drowned chapel.

salt_saint_elsbeth_after: Elsbeth: La la laaa. Twelve years of the same hymn. I hate this hymn.

lines: Saint Elsbeth: The Salt Saint? That's me. Alive. Kaspar is my brother. He sells kitchen salt in little bags and I sing down here so pilgrims hear it.
Elsbeth: We split it sixty-forty. I asked for fifty-fifty. He said saints don't need money. Tell him I'm done being dead.

salt_saint_kaspar_salt_after: Kaspar: Elsbeth sings above ground now. Fifty-fifty. Business has never been worse.

lines: You take Kaspar's relic box: three revival leaves under a false bottom and a receipt for forty sacks of kitchen salt.
salt_saint_kaspar_salt_loot.action: set_flag q4_salt_saint_paid; give_item revival_leaf 3; quest_stage q4_salt_saint 4

salt_saint_kaspar_salt_defeat: Kaspar: Fine. Fifty-fifty. Tell her. No, wait, don't tell her I said fine.
Kaspar: Take my last bags. They're real salt, at least. Kitchen-blessed.
salt_saint_kaspar_salt_lose: Kaspar: Rest, pilgrim. Salt heals all wounds. It also stings.

lines: Kaspar: Every saint needs a martyr. You'll do. I'll sell your boots as relics.

agnes: Agnes: I sweep the Long Stair top to bottom. The Gilt House sweeps people the same way.
agnes_intro: Agnes: You're standing in my dust. Fight or shift.
lenz: Lenz: I paint the cloud shadows before they move. The Gilt House buys the paintings to prove they own the weather.
lenz_intro: Lenz: Hold still, you're in the composition. And now you're in a fight.
lenz_defeat: Lenz: Smudged. I'll call it modern.
sigrun: Sigrun: I walk the salt where it's thinnest, for practice. Practice for what, nobody asks.
sigrun_intro: Sigrun: You've got heavy feet. Let's test the salt with you.
sigrun_defeat: Sigrun: Still standing. Both of us. Disappointing.
oswin: Oswin: Every brass screw that falls off the Orrery is worth a meal. I've eaten very well this year.
oswin_intro: Oswin: You're after my screws. Everyone is.
oswin_defeat: Oswin: Take a screw. Just one. A loose one.
bruna: Bruna: I tread the Gilt grapes barefoot. The family says it adds character. The doctor says it adds fungus.
bruna_intro: Bruna: You walked on my vines. Now I walk on you.
bruna_defeat: Bruna: Pressed flat. That's my job, not yours.
hedda: Hedda: I inspect the Span ropes. I pass them all. Veronne pays me per pass, the families pay me per fail.
hedda_intro: Hedda: Let's see how much strain you take.
hedda_defeat: Hedda: Passed. Don't let it go to your head.
thea: Thea: The planet fell, the crater stayed. I sell crater by the bucket. Very fashionable in Gildcrest gardens.
thea_intro: Thea: This hole is mine. Dig your own.
thea_defeat: Thea: Fine. Have a bucket. Bring it back.
moritz: Moritz: Isaura says stars come loose under the Orrery. I'm here with a net. So far: two moths and a hat.
moritz_intro: Moritz: You scared off my star. Fight me.
moritz_defeat: Moritz: Caught out. Not a star in sight.
bendix: Bendix: I took a vow of silence. Then a vow of salt. The silence was easier.
bendix_defeat: Bendix: Ow. There. I said a word. Happy?
wiebke: Wiebke: I keep the chapel font full. Halloran's barrels keep it empty. We have an arrangement. It involves shouting.
wiebke_intro: Wiebke: Are you with the barrels? You look like you're with the barrels.
wiebke_defeat: Wiebke: Not with the barrels, then. Sorry. Here, holy water. Mostly.
tilman: Tilman: I guard the Gilt Cellars. Mostly from the family. They drink the good years and refill them with the bad ones.
tilman_intro: Tilman: Nobody comes down here without a reason. Let's hear yours. In battle.
tilman_defeat: Tilman: Fair. Mind cask forty-one. It knocks.
edeltraud: Edeltraud: The strongroom holds the Gilt gold, the Gilt wills and the Gilt grudges. The grudges take the most space.
edeltraud_intro: Edeltraud: Visitors sign in. In battle.
edeltraud_defeat: Edeltraud: Signed. Don't touch anything. Especially the wills. They bite.
